quest.title: A Boy's Letter
quest.description: Draff of Springvale seems to be fretting over a letter...

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: *sigh* I wonder how the kid's getting along...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Hmm...? Oh, hi. Perfect timing, do you still remember that letter from last time?

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: If you can spare the time, please deliver this letter to Grace for me.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Well, I'm hardly going to trust those pigeons with it after what happened last time.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Also, if I take the letter to Mondstadt myself, I'll have to face that kid...

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: *sigh* Don't ask... Just... Please. Do this for me.

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: Strange, it should be here by now... What if something's happened...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A letter for you, from Draff.

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: Hmm? What are you doing here? You're not a carrier pigeon...

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: ...Something happened to the pigeons? Goodness. Never a dull day in Springvale.

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: Well, thanks for bringing the letter. One second, I've got a little something for you in return...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the letter...

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: Oh, you read it? Not that it matters, it's nothing confidential.

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: To put it in Draff's words, it's just something that happened a long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: But although it was long ago, it's something we will never forget.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please continue...

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: You really want to know? Well, you seem trustworthy enough... But promise me you will keep it a secret.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: ...Timmie's father is good friends with Draff. They do everything together — hunting, drinking, causing all sorts of trouble...

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: I don't know how many times they've been warned by the Knights. Or been lectured by Sister Victoria.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: Finally, when Timmie was born, his father reined it in. Went teetotal and everything. Started working hard to provide for his family and "set an example" for his son, as he puts it.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: He became so obsessed with not setting a bad example for Timmie that he even managed to get Draff to give up alcohol.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: ...Except that once in a while, when they just couldn't bear it anymore, they'd meet up and binge drink apple cider. I joined them for a drink too, once or twice.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: Unfortunately, Timmie's father was seriously injured in a hunting accident one day...

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: Draff brought him here as quickly as he could, and we did everything within our power to save him... But sadly, he didn't make it.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: Since then, Draff's asked me to look after Timmie while he returns to Springvale to be a hunter.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: Each month he sends a letter and some money. But he can't face seeing Timmie.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: Recently, he has started saying he wants to tell Timmie the truth about that fateful day... *sigh* I dread to think what he must have been through...

choices.text: You don't want Timmie to know the truth?

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: Correct. He's still just a child... I don't think it's wise to tell him everything.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: As much as he says he's a big boy now, and even helps me look after Nora and Glory...

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: ...I'm just not sure he could cope with all the gruesome details. It's too much.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: Maybe when he's older. But for now...

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: I'd rather he has the chance of a happy childhood. Even if that means not being completely honest with him.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: I won't deny that Timmie is growing up, though. He's increasingly curious, and asks more and more questions...

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: It's getting more and more difficult for me to face him.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: Nora says Timmie always used to drag her out into the wild, saying he wanted to make a gift for his father or send a letter to him.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: But these days, he's so sullen and lifeless all the time.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: If you have the time, could you check up on Timmie for me?

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: Wonderful, thanks.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: It's awkward, but... Although I keep saying to myself I won't tell him the truth...

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: ...Every time I hear him say he wants to write a letter to his father, my heart goes out to him.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: I'm worried that one day I won't be able to stop myself from telling him the whole story.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: ...I won't let that happen.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: So please go and check up on Timmie on my behalf.

choices.text: You can't hide it from him forever.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: I know that, I do... But he's just so young...

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: I just hope... No, I insist that he has the chance of a happy childhood.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: That way, whatever awful things he might experience in life, at the very least he will have some fond memories to look back on.

choices.text: What's so bad about knowing the truth?

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: Hmm... Well, it makes sense for someone like you to think that way. You've been through a lot already, which has given you courage and resilience.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: I have no doubt that whatever has shaped you into who you are today, it must have included some very painful experiences.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: But Timmie is still so young. Maybe it is out of my own selfishness, but I won't have him taking on more than he can bear.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: ...At the very least, I want him to have a happy childhood.

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: Ugh, you are insufferable...

response.speaker: Grace
response.text: ...But go on then.

dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: ...Still no news. Not even a word.

response.speaker: Timmie
response.text: I fed them already today. And I got them to fly away earlier, so they would be safe... from you.

response.speaker: Timmie
response.text: Now I'm writing a letter.

response.speaker: Timmie
response.text: Mommy says that Daddy will send a letter by pigeon when he has time.

response.speaker: Timmie
response.text: But I've waited and waited and I haven't had a single letter from him... Maybe Daddy's just too busy at work.

response.speaker: Timmie
response.text: Since Daddy's too busy, I want to send him a letter first. With a nice gift inside. But what would make a good gift?

response.speaker: Timmie
response.text: ...I got it! <color=#00E1FFFF>Dandelions</color>. Mommy says everyone in Mondstadt loves Dandelions.

response.speaker: Timmie
response.text: Do you have time to find me some <color=#00E1FFFF>Dandelions</color>?

response.speaker: Timmie
response.text: Yay! Thank you! ...So you ARE nice sometimes...

response.speaker: Timmie
response.text: I did wanna send something better, but if it's too heavy the pigeon won't be able to carry it.

response.speaker: Timmie
response.text: And Daddy works reeeeeally far away... The pigeon will have a long way to go already.

response.speaker: Timmie
response.text: Writing a letter to Daddy.

dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: Did you get my Dandelions?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Got them.

dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: Yay! This is plenty.

dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: In go the Dandelion Seeds... now I seal the envelope...

dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: ...And we're all set! Yay! Daddy's going to be so happy when he gets my letter.

dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: But... I heard that you need to use a proper trained carrier pigeon when you wanna send a letter. And I don't know Daddy's address...

dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: Oh wait — I just remembered, Mommy says that Mr. Draff from Springvale keeps carrier pigeons.

dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: And she also says that Mr. Draff knows Daddy. He must be able to send this letter.

dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: So... Can you help me again? Take this letter to Mr. Draff and get him to send it to Daddy for me.

dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: One more thing — no peeking!

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: You're back? Did you deliver the letter?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Timmie wants you to send this letter to his daddy.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Timmie's still writing letters to his father... I assume you heard the whole story from Grace.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: I... I can't send this.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Well, yes... As much as I'd like to, I simply can't.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: There's nothing I can do. I suppose I'll just hold onto it for now.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Anyway, enough about that. I will keep the letter. Please consider it sent.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: He would understand... My dear old friend.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Thanks for your help and please, please don't tell Timmie about this. I can trust you with that, right? ...Considering, here's your payment...

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Hahaha... That's the adventurer in you talking! Decisive and efficient in all things.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: I'm no adventurer myself. Just a plain old hunter.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: I'm not going to burn this, or even open it. I'm just going to hold onto it for now.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: What for? Surely you don't think my old friend might still be alive...

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: ...Somewhere, out there, just waiting to be found...

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Yes, I used to wonder the same thing myself. Even put it to the test, but...

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: In the end I just had to accept the facts — my best friend is gone forever, never to return.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: ...I thought you were supposed to be delivering my letter?

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: ...It's about something that happened a long time ago. I take it you didn't read it last time, then?

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Don't bother reading it. It's boring and long-winded.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: If you must know, I mean that little boy who's always feeding the pigeons on the bridge.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Yes, Timmie. For certain reasons... it would be best if I avoided him at the moment.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Happy now? Now quickly, get this letter to Grace before she starts fretting.

dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: Anyway. Go get me some <color=#00E1FFFF>Dandelions</color>! You promised. And I've nearly finished writing my letter.

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: ...Lord Barbatos, if you've been watching...

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: ...Please tell me what I'm supposed to do.

dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: Remember, give it to Mr. Draff in Springvale. Don't give it to the wrong person!

dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: Mommy says Daddy and him are best friends. He's sure to know how to get this letter to Daddy.

dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: But... Mommy also says that Mr. Draff and Daddy are both very busy in their work... Hmm, I wonder if I'll be busy like them when I grow up...

dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: Ah, it doesn't matter — as long as I get to help Daddy, I don't mind if it's busy.
